analysis.investment_thesis: H.G. Infra is a genuine beneficiary of India's infrastructure boom with an exceptional 9-year PAT CAGR of 36.8% and a dirt-cheap forward P/E of 7.4x, but a dangerous debt explosion in FY2025 (borrowings up 3.7x YoY to ₹5,669 Cr) and persistently negative operating cash flow for 4 of 5 years make this a watch-and-wait rather than a high-conviction buy.
key_strengths: Phenomenal historical compounding — Revenue 23.8% CAGR, PAT 36.8% CAGR over 9 years, with operating margins a healthy 18.6%
Structural tailwind — roads, highways, railways, solar; classic India infra spending cycle beneficiary
Promoter conviction — 71.78% holding, stable, no apparent dilution agenda
key_risks: Debt has gone parabolic — borrowings ballooned from ₹1,513 Cr (FY24) to ₹5,669 Cr (FY25) in a single year; D/E now 1.83x vs my comfort ceiling of 0.6x
Cash flow structurally broken — OCF negative in 4 of last 5 years, FCF hit -₹2,415 Cr in FY25; finance costs at ₹265 Cr consume 52% of PAT
Revenue and PAT actually declined in FY25 (₹5,056 Cr vs ₹5,378 Cr; ₹505 Cr vs ₹539 Cr) — first decline in history, raising execution concerns
red_flags: FY2025 balance sheet looks transformed — total assets nearly doubled to ₹10,394 Cr with CWIP surging from ₹14 Cr to ₹1,322 Cr; HAM project equity commitments are creating a debt trap
Free cash flow negative every single year for 5 years — this is not a temporary working capital blip, it is structural to the HAM model and signals the business consumes rather than generates cash
Interest burden growing at 36.6% CAGR — same rate as PAT CAGR; if revenue growth stalls further, interest coverage deteriorates rapidly
analysis.detailed_analysis:
H.G. Infra is a well-run Rajasthan-based EPC contractor that has ridden India's road and highway capex supercycle brilliantly — the 9-year numbers are genuinely impressive. At P/E 10.6x and forward P/E 7.4x with P/B of just 1.32x, the market is pricing in significant skepticism, which a contrarian investor could exploit. Promoter holding at 71.78% demonstrates skin in the game and is reassuring on governance. The pivot toward Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) projects, solar, and railways gives the company diversification that pure road EPC players lack.

However, what happened in FY2025 demands serious scrutiny. Borrowings jumped from ₹1,513 Cr to ₹5,669 Cr in a single year — an increase of ₹4,156 Cr — largely to fund HAM equity commitments (CWIP alone jumped ₹1,308 Cr). This model generates annuity cash flows over 15 years but bleeds cash during construction; OCF hit -₹878 Cr and FCF -₹2,415 Cr in FY25. A business that earns ₹505 Cr net profit but burns ₹2,415 Cr in free cash flow is not yet investable at high conviction — I need to see revenue recover above ₹5,400 Cr and OCF turn positive before adding meaningfully. Watch the order book, HAM project milestones, and whether FY26 debt stabilises — if debt plateaus and annuity income starts flowing, the re-rating could be sharp.
